title: Project 1: Plant Nursery
description: Learn the commercial and ecological essentials of raising healthy plants from seeds, cuttings, and saplings. Students survey local nurseries, design shade-net nursery layouts, prepare soil-compost growing media, master seed germination, nurture saplings, and calculate costs and pricing.

activities.title: Activity 1: Visit to a nearby plant nursery
activities.material_required: Field notebook, pen, camera, survey questionnaire.
activities.description: Visit a commercial or forest plant nursery. Observe propagation areas, mother beds, seedling trays, mist chambers, and shade nets. Interview nursery growers regarding seasonal plant demand, propagation methods (seeds, stem cuttings, grafting), and watering routines.

activities.title: Activity 2: Planning and laying out a plant nursery
activities.material_required: Graph paper, measuring tape, scale, markers, layout reference.
activities.description: Form groups to survey the school campus and sketch a scaled nursery layout plan. Demarcate mother beds, potting shed, shade-net zone, water source, pathways, and tool storage.

activities.title: Activity 3: Preparing land and setting up shade-net
activities.material_required: Bamboo poles, shade netting (50% or 75% green), coir string, spade, trowel, garden soil, vermicompost, sand.
activities.description: Clear ground, level nursery beds, erect bamboo frame, and secure shade-netting to protect young seedlings from scorching sun and heavy downpours. Prepare a 1:1:1 potting mix of topsoil, sand, and organic compost.

activities.title: Activity 4: Germinating seeds and rooting cuttings
activities.material_required: Seedling trays / pro-trays, cocopeat, vermiculite, vegetable/flower seeds, healthy stem cuttings, root hormone (optional), water mister.
activities.description: Fill seedling trays with moist cocopeat. Sow seeds at uniform depths and insert semi-hardwood stem cuttings at 45-degree angles. Maintain moisture using gentle water misting.

activities.title: Activity 5: Raising and potting plants in the nursery
activities.material_required: Poly-grow bags (various sizes), potting media, young seedlings, trowel, watering can with rose head.
activities.description: Transplant vigorous saplings from germination trays into labelled poly-bags filled with enriched potting soil. Tamp soil gently around roots, water thoroughly, and arrange bags in orderly nursery rows.

activities.title: Activity 6: Watching plants grow and nursery maintenance
activities.material_required: Growth logbook, ruler, neem oil organic biopesticide sprayer, pruners.
activities.description: Monitor plant height, leaf count, branching, and root development weekly. Weed poly-bags, pinch shoot tips to encourage bushy growth, and spray organic neem biopesticide at the first sign of pests.

activities.title: Activity 7: Calculating nursery costs and selling saplings
activities.material_required: Expense ledger, calculator, price tags, sale display table.
activities.description: Total all expenses incurred (seeds, poly-bags, cocopeat, shade-netting, manure). Calculate cost price per healthy sapling, fix a fair selling price with profit margin, and organize a School Plant Sale.

title: Project 2: School Habitat Garden
description: Design and build a vibrant micro-habitat garden in the school campus that provides food, water, and shelter for local birds, butterflies, pollinators, and beneficial creatures.

activities.title: Activity 1: Identifying animals and birds in and around the school
activities.material_required: Binoculars, notebook, camera, local bird & butterfly field guide.
activities.description: Observe and record the birds, butterflies, squirrels, dragonflies, bees, and earthworms that visit or live on campus. Note their feeding habits, roosting spots, and seasonal activity patterns.

activities.title: Activity 2: Interaction with an ecological expert
activities.material_required: Interview questionnaire, voice recorder/notepad.
activities.description: Interview a wildlife naturalist, ornithologist, or forestry expert on how to create micro-habitats, attract native pollinators, and choose host plants for local butterflies.

activities.title: Activity 3: Identifying natural habitats and micro-zones
activities.material_required: Campus map, clipboard, coloured pencils.
activities.description: Identify potential micro-habitats across school grounds: sunny rockeries, quiet shaded tree canopies, moist damp corners, and open flower corridors.

activities.title: Activity 4: Identifying needs of local wildlife species
activities.material_required: Chart paper, markers, species requirement chart.
activities.description: Create a wildlife needs matrix detailing essential food (nectar, seeds, fruits), water sources (bird baths, shallow mud puddles), and nesting/shelter requirements for target species.

activities.title: Activity 5: Designing the habitat garden layout
activities.material_required: Graph paper, drafting tools, list of native nectar & caterpillar host plants (Milkweed, Curry leaf, Hibiscus, Lantana, Citrus).
activities.description: Design a master plan for the school habitat garden including a butterfly nectar zone, caterpillar host plant patch, bird bath, log pile for insects, and stone basking wall.

activities.title: Activity 6: Creating the habitat garden
activities.material_required: Spades, trowels, saplings of nectar and host plants, terracotta bird bath, stones, dry logs, mulch.
activities.description: Dig planting beds, plant pollinator-friendly flora, install shallow earthen bird baths with landing perches, construct rockeries and insect hotels, and spread organic mulch.

activities.title: Activity 7: Observing occupants of the habitat garden
activities.material_required: Observation journal, magnifying glass, camera.
activities.description: Conduct quiet morning observations. Record new butterfly species laying eggs on host plants, caterpillar feeding stages, bird bath visitors, and pollinator interactions.

activities.title: Activity 8: Maintaining the habitat garden
activities.material_required: Watering hose, fresh water for bird baths, shears.
activities.description: Refill clean water in bird baths daily to prevent mosquito breeding. Prune withered branches, remove invasive weeds, and top up mulch layer.

activities.title: Activity 9: Showcasing your habitat garden and community awareness
activities.material_required: Signboards, painted plant markers, exhibition display board, visitor register.
activities.description: Install educational labels describing each plant and the wildlife it supports. Lead guided tours for junior classes, parents, and community members.

title: Project 3: Tie and Dye (Bandhani)
part: Part 2: Work with Machines and Materials
description: Master the traditional textile craft of resist dyeing (Tie and Dye / Bandhani). Students explore cultural textile traditions, learn folding and binding techniques, prepare dye solutions, create wearable artefacts, and analyze production costs.

activities.title: Activity 1: Visit to a textile craft shop or artisan emporium
activities.material_required: Notepad, pen, camera, sample swatch analysis sheet.
activities.description: Visit a traditional handloom store or Bandhani emporium. Examine tie and dye patterns (Leheriya, Mothra, Shikari, Shibori, Spiral, Sunburst) and interview artisans on fabrics and dyes.

activities.title: Activity 2: A visit to a tie and dye workshop
activities.material_required: Survey notepad, safety glasses (for observation).
activities.description: Observe professional master dyers. Note how fabric is scoured, tied tightly with cotton thread, immersed in cold/hot dye baths, fixed with salt/alum mordants, and washed to reveal patterns.

activities.title: Activity 3: Exploring techniques of folding, tying, and dyeing swatches
activities.material_required: White cotton fabric swatches (10x10 inch), rubber bands, thread, marbles, ice cream sticks, cold water fabric dyes, table salt, squeeze bottles, plastic gloves, apron.
activities.description: Experiment with different resist techniques: Accordion fold (stripes/Leheriya), Spiral twist (swirls), Bullseye (circles using marbles and rubber bands), and clamping with wooden sticks (Itajime Shibori). Apply vibrant dyes and observe colour blending.

activities.title: Activity 4: Making the final product (T-shirt, Stole, or Tote Bag)
activities.material_required: Plain white cotton T-shirt / stole / canvas bag, dye powders, fixative, washing basin, drying rack.
activities.description: Apply your mastered binding design to a full-size wearable item. Tie tightly, dye with precision, allow 24 hours curing in plastic wrap, rinse thoroughly until water runs clear, and iron flat.

activities.title: Activity 5: Cost calculation and marketing your textile product
activities.material_required: Calculator, product tags, packaging bags, craft fair display board.
activities.description: Calculate raw material costs (fabric, dye, fixative, packaging). Determine selling price considering labour value, attach a designer wash-care tag, and display at the School Craft Bazaar.

title: Project 4: AI Assistant
part: Part 2: Work with Machines and Materials
description: Understand Artificial Intelligence fundamentals through hands-on model training. Students explore computer vision, speech recognition, and machine learning, train an image/sound classifier using Teachable Machine, and build an interactive AI Assistant.

activities.title: Activity 1: Human vs Machine: Who is Better at What?
activities.material_required: Activity worksheet, comparison chart, computer / smart board.
activities.description: Compare human cognitive abilities with computational strengths. Explore patterns, calculations, emotions, creativity, and memory across biological and artificial intelligence.

activities.title: Activity 2: AI can see, listen, and speak - Exploring AI Perception
activities.material_required: Computer with webcam and microphone, browser access to AI demo tools (Quick Draw, AutoDraw, Speech-to-Text).
activities.description: Interact with online AI perception demos. Test how neural networks interpret doodle sketches in milliseconds and transcribe spoken regional accents.

activities.title: Activity 3: Is AI creative? Exploring generative art and text
activities.material_required: Computer / tablet, generative AI sandboxes.
activities.description: Explore AI music, image, and poem generation. Discuss prompts, style transfer, and the difference between algorithmic imitation and genuine human emotional creativity.

activities.title: Activity 4: Preparing to design your own AI Assistant
activities.material_required: Design storyboard, problem statement worksheet.
activities.description: Define the purpose of your AI Assistant: e.g. Waste Sorting Assistant (Bio vs Plastic), Plant Disease Classifier, or Gesture-Controlled Classroom Signaler.

activities.title: Activity 5: Teaching the machine to recognise images (Data Collection)
activities.material_required: Google Teachable Machine / Scratch AI extension, webcam, sample physical objects for classes.
activities.description: Create distinct image classes in Teachable Machine. Capture 100+ webcam training images per class across diverse lighting angles, backgrounds, and distances.

activities.title: Activity 6: Training the neural model for recognition
activities.material_required: Browser, Teachable Machine training panel.
activities.description: Train the machine learning model. Understand epochs, learning rate, and batch size. Observe how the classifier calculates real-time confidence scores.

activities.title: Activity 7: Testing and improving the AI model (Handling Bias & Edge Cases)
activities.material_required: Test objects, confidence score logbook.
activities.description: Test the trained model with unseen objects and edge cases. Identify misclassifications, retrain with augmented dataset, and eliminate dataset bias.

activities.title: Activity 8: Making the AI Assistant interactive with code
activities.material_required: Scratch / Block coding environment with Teachable Machine extension.
activities.description: Export the model into Scratch. Code custom responses: when camera detects 'Plastic Waste', sprite plays audio alert and displays green recycling bin animation.

activities.title: Activity 9: Sharing your AI Assistant and discussing AI Ethics
activities.material_required: Project presentation slides, AI ethics debate prompts.
activities.description: Demonstrate your AI assistant to classmates. Discuss ethical questions: privacy, surveillance, automation jobs, and responsible AI use.

title: Project 5: Storytime with Puppets
description: Harness the power of theatrical storytelling through puppetry. Students analyze story structures, craft puppets (shadow, glove, rod, or marionette), build miniature stage sets, write scripts, and stage a live puppet show.

activities.title: Activity 1: What makes stories work? Understanding narrative structure
activities.material_required: Folk tale books, story mountain template worksheet.
activities.description: Deconstruct beloved Panchatantra, Jataka, or local folk tales. Identify introduction, conflict, rising action, climax, and resolution.

activities.title: Activity 2: Watching a puppet show and analyzing techniques
activities.material_required: Video projector, puppet performance analysis sheet.
activities.description: Watch classical Indian puppetry traditions (Kathputli, Tholu Bommalata, Tolpava Koothu, glove puppets). Observe voice modulation, lighting, and puppet manipulation mechanisms.

activities.title: Activity 3: Selecting and adapting a story for puppets
activities.material_required: Story drafting sheets, pens.
activities.description: Choose a compelling theme (environmental conservation, honesty, teamwork) and adapt it into a fast-paced 5-minute puppet play.

activities.title: Activity 4: Writing a script for the puppet show
activities.material_required: Script templates, highlighters.
activities.description: Write dialogue scripts with character cues, stage directions, background music hints, and sound effect annotations.

activities.title: Activity 5: Character sketch and puppet visualization
activities.material_required: Drawing sheets, colored pencils, character personality profile cards.
activities.description: Draw full-color sketches of each puppet character, detailing expressions, costume colors, and movement mechanics.

activities.title: Activity 6: Making puppets (Glove, Rod, and Shadow Puppets)
activities.material_required: Socks, discarded cardboard, fabric scraps, wool yarn, googly eyes, wooden dowels, wire, glue gun, scissors.
activities.description: Construct working puppets using upcycled materials. Build glove puppets with movable mouths, shadow puppets with articulated limbs on rods, and yarn hair.

activities.title: Activity 7: Building the stage, lighting, and sound effects
activities.material_required: Large carton box, translucent white fabric (for shadow screen), flashlight / desk lamp, percussion instruments (bells, shakers).
activities.description: Construct a collapsible tabletop puppet theatre. Install side curtains, shadow projection backdrop, and sound effect stations.

activities.title: Activity 8: Rehearsing and putting up a live puppet show
activities.material_required: Puppet stage, puppets, audience seats, show invitations.
activities.description: Rehearse voice projection, puppet synchronization, and lighting transitions. Perform the live show before an audience of primary students and teachers.

title: Project 6: Family Health Handbook
description: Empower students as community health ambassadors. Students explore disease prevention, compile emergency first-aid kits, conduct family health surveys across age groups, analyze nutritional habits, and build an actionable Family Health Plan.

activities.title: Activity 1: Factors Affecting Health (Physical, Mental & Environmental)
activities.material_required: Health determinant chart, sticky notes, markers.
activities.description: Brainstorm factors influencing health: balanced nutrition, physical activity, clean water, sleep hygiene, emotional well-being, and pollution exposure.

activities.title: Activity 2: Framing health survey questions for your family
activities.material_required: Survey questionnaire template, clipboard.
activities.description: Develop a respectful family health questionnaire covering daily water intake, exercise, fruit/vegetable consumption, screen time, vaccination records, and medical checkups.

activities.title: Activity 3: Visit to a Hospital / Primary Health Centre (PHC)
activities.material_required: Field notebook, pen, interview checklist.
activities.description: Visit a local PHC or community clinic. Interact with medical officers, nurses, and ASHA workers to understand immunisation schedules, epidemic prevention, and basic triage.

activities.title: Activity 4: Creating a comprehensive home First-Aid Kit
activities.material_required: First-aid box container, sterile gauze, bandages, antiseptic lotion (Dettol/Betadine), burn ointment, ORS packets, thermometer, medical scissors, emergency contact list.
activities.description: Assemble an emergency first-aid kit with proper labelling. Practice basic first-aid protocols: cleaning abrasions, dressing cuts, applying cold compresses, and preparing ORS solutions.

activities.title: Activity 5: Factors affecting health at different age groups (Infants, Youth, Elders)
activities.material_required: Age-group health matrix, chart paper.
activities.description: Analyze health priorities across life stages: infant immunisations, adolescent posture and nutrition, adult stress management, and geriatric joint/blood pressure care.

activities.title: Activity 6: Analysing survey data of family members
activities.material_required: Completed family health survey sheets, calculator, colored highlighters.
activities.description: Tabulate survey data. Calculate average family water intake, identify nutrient deficiencies (low iron/calcium), and pinpoint sedentary habits.

activities.title: Activity 7: Making a Family Health & Wellness Action Plan
activities.material_required: Handbook template sheets, binding clips.
activities.description: Create a personalized Family Health Handbook featuring dietary recommendations, weekly exercise goals, vaccination trackers, and doctor contact numbers.

activities.title: Activity 8: Environmental health and vector prevention in the neighborhood
activities.material_required: Neighborhood checklist, awareness posters, safe disposal bags.
activities.description: Conduct a neighborhood audit to eliminate stagnant water puddles (mosquito breeding control), ensure proper household waste segregation, and promote clean drinking water storage.
